prm:groups.label: When I’m emotionally overwhelmed but can

prm:prompts.text: I’m feeling something strong but I can’t identify it clearly. Help me slow it down and separate the physical sensations, emotions, thoughts, fears, and meanings I’m attaching to what’s happening. Don’t try to fix anything yet.
prm:prompts.title: When I’m emotionally overwhelmed but can’t name what I’m feeling

prm:prompts.text: My mind is generating too many thoughts at once. I’m going to dump everything here. Help me separate facts, fears, predictions, assumptions, decisions, and things that don’t actually require my attention right now: [brain dump]
prm:prompts.title: When my mind won’t stop racing

prm:prompts.text: I’m overwhelmed by [situation]. Separate this into what I control, what I can influence, what I can prepare for, and what is completely outside my control. Then help me redirect my attention toward my actual agency.
prm:prompts.title: When I need to figure out what’s mine to carry

prm:prompts.text: I’m letting [person/their opinion/their reaction] affect me more than I want. Help me identify what authority I’ve unconsciously given them, what information from them is genuinely useful, and what I do not need to internalize.
prm:prompts.title: When I’m giving someone else too much power

prm:prompts.text: I’m feeling insecure about [thing]. Don’t immediately reassure me. Help me understand what the insecurity is protecting, what standard or desire is underneath it, whether any useful information is contained in it, and how I could consciously direct that energy.
prm:prompts.title: When I feel insecure

prm:prompts.text: I’m procrastinating on [task/goal]. Don’t assume I need more discipline. Help me diagnose the friction. Explore whether the problem is fear, unclear next steps, low perceived reward, perfectionism, identity conflict, overwhelm, lack of energy, lack of meaning, or something else.
prm:prompts.title: When I’m procrastinating

prm:prompts.text: I’m using a lot of force to make myself do [thing]. Help me understand why there is so much internal resistance and what could create greater alignment without simply lowering my standards.
prm:prompts.title: When I keep forcing myself

prm:prompts.text: I noticed myself falling into this old pattern again: [pattern]. Help me examine it as an automatic program rather than proof that I haven’t changed. Identify the trigger, belief, emotional reward, behavior, and alternative response I could practice.
prm:prompts.title: When an old pattern resurfaces

prm:prompts.text: A part of me is saying: [doubt]. Don’t argue with it or reassure me that it’s wrong. Help me observe it, understand what experience or prediction it may be based on, and determine what useful information—if any—it contains.
prm:prompts.title: When doubt appears

prm:prompts.text: There’s a part of myself I keep trying to get rid of: [trait/emotion/desire]. Help me explore what its destructive expression looks like, what its useful expression might look like, and how I could integrate it rather than either suppressing or obeying it.
prm:prompts.title: When I need to integrate rather than suppress something

prm:prompts.text: I keep telling myself I need more certainty about [decision]. Help me identify what information is truly necessary before acting versus what I’m using as an excuse to postpone uncertainty.
prm:prompts.title: When I want certainty before acting

prm:prompts.text: I’ve been planning [goal] for a while. Help me determine whether my planning is still creating useful clarity or has become psychologically respectable procrastination. What could I only learn by taking action now?
prm:prompts.title: When I’m overplanning

prm:prompts.text: Here is everything I currently know about [situation]. Give me the smallest meaningful action that would produce new information, reduce uncertainty, or create momentum.
prm:prompts.title: When I need an actionable next move

prm:prompts.text: I’m interpreting [result] as failure. Help me analyze it like an experiment instead. What did I expect, what actually happened, what information did I gain, what assumption changed, and what should I test next?
prm:prompts.title: When I feel like I failed

prm:prompts.text: My next chapter is centered around [goal/season]. Help me design an identity for it. I want traits, beliefs, standards, behaviors, boundaries, default responses, and things this version of me no longer does.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to define my next identity

prm:prompts.text: Help me turn my future self from an abstract concept into someone psychologically specific. Interview me about their ordinary routines, standards, environment, relationships, work, internal dialogue, emotional patterns, decisions, and worldview.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to make my future self concrete

prm:prompts.text: Here is the person I want to become: [description]. Help me distinguish between behaviors that would merely make me look like this person and behaviors that would actually build the underlying identity.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to embody instead of perform

prm:prompts.text: Based on these things I’ve done recently: [list], help me identify what they reveal about my emerging identity. Turn them into evidence-based statements about who I am becoming without exaggerating them.
prm:prompts.title: When I want proof that I’m already changing

prm:prompts.text: Interview me and help me construct an ordinary day in the life I’m creating. Focus less on luxury or impressive outcomes and more on what I see, do, feel, think about, create, tolerate, refuse, and consider normal.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to create a vivid future scene

prm:prompts.text: My current goal is [goal]. Show me what 3x, 10x, and radically unconstrained versions of this goal could look like. Then help me identify which assumptions would have to change at each level.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to think bigger

prm:prompts.text: Here is the life/result I’m envisioning: [vision]. Reverse-engineer it into identity, capabilities, systems, relationships, resources, decisions, and actions rather than simply giving me a to-do list.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to reverse-engineer a vision

prm:prompts.text: Here is everything currently competing for my attention: [list]. Help me sort it into essential, valuable, optional, noise, and actively harmful to my focus.
prm:prompts.title: When I feel mentally scattered

prm:prompts.text: My primary vision right now is [vision]. Based on that, help me create an attention filter: what should receive more attention, what should receive less, and what should rarely be allowed into my mental environment?
prm:prompts.title: When I need to protect my attention

prm:prompts.text: I’m unsure whether [idea] will work. Help me design the smallest useful experiment that can generate real evidence within [time period].
prm:prompts.title: When I want to test an idea instead of debate it forever

prm:prompts.text: Instead of giving me generic habit advice, help me treat [habit] as an experiment. Identify triggers, environment, friction, reward, identity, and one variable to change first.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to change a habit

prm:prompts.text: I’ve researched [topic] extensively but still haven’t acted. Based on what I know, identify which remaining questions truly need answers and which can only be answered through experience.
prm:prompts.title: When I’m stuck researching

prm:prompts.text: I’m fascinated by [topic]. Give me 15 increasingly strange, deep, interdisciplinary questions I could follow rather than simply explaining the topic to me.
prm:prompts.title: When I want a rabbit hole

prm:prompts.text: Here are subjects I currently care about: [subjects]. Give me five surprising connections between them that could send me into genuinely interesting rabbit holes.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to blow my own mind

prm:prompts.text: I don’t want a productivity task right now. I want intellectual or creative nourishment. Based on [current fascination], give me things to contemplate, notice, research, collect, experience, or create.
prm:prompts.title: When I need creative nourishment rather than productivity

prm:prompts.text: I think I want [activity/path], but I’ve mostly experienced the idea of it rather than the reality. Help me design a low-risk experiment that exposes me to the real experience.
prm:prompts.title: When I want to test whether I actually enjoy something

prm:prompts.text: Show me how [problem] looks when viewed as a moment, a pattern, a learning period, a chapter, and one small part of a much longer life.
prm:prompts.title: When I need a wider frame

prm:prompts.text: Here is a question I’m interested in: [question]. Give me ten increasingly unusual questions hidden underneath it.
prm:prompts.title: When I want stranger questions
